title: LED Circuit
subtitle: Basic breadboard circuit with resistor & LED
next_action: Insert the 220Ω resistor into the breadboard
description: Build a simple LED circuit using a breadboard, resistor, LED, and jumper wires. Learn basic pin header connections and current limiting.

physical_attributes.orientation_marker: Long lead is anode (positive). Flat edge on housing marks cathode (negative).

steps.title: Insert 220Ω Resistor
steps.instruction: Place the 220Ω resistor bridging Row 10 to Row 15 across the center divider of the breadboard.

common_mistakes.explanation: The resistor right lead is inserted into Row 14 instead of Row 15.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Shift the right lead one slot down from Row 14 to Row 15.

common_mistakes.condition: Both leads on same side of divider
common_mistakes.explanation: Both resistor leads are on the same half of the breadboard. The resistor must bridge across the center divider.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Move one lead to the opposite side so the resistor crosses the center channel.

steps.title: Insert 100µF Capacitor
steps.instruction: Insert the 100µF electrolytic capacitor into the C2 header slot, observing polarity. The white stripe (negative) faces the GND rail.

common_mistakes.explanation: The capacitor polarity is reversed. The white stripe should face the GND rail.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Rotate the capacitor 180 degrees so the white stripe aligns with the ground rail.

steps.title: Connect LED Anode to Node 12A
steps.instruction: Align the long lead (anode) of the red LED with pin 12A on the breadboard.

orientation_constraints.rule: Long lead (anode) inserted into Row 12A. Flat edge on housing faces away from resistor.

common_mistakes.explanation: The LED leads are reversed. The longer lead (anode) should go into pin 12A.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Remove the LED and reinsert with the long lead in pin 12A.

steps.title: Place Current Limiting Resistor
steps.instruction: Bridge the current limiting resistor from pin 12B to the ground rail.

common_mistakes.condition: Connected to VCC rail instead of GND
common_mistakes.explanation: The resistor is connected to the positive VCC rail instead of the ground rail.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Move the lead from the red VCC rail to the blue GND rail.

steps.title: Insert Ground Jumper Wire
steps.instruction: Connect a black jumper wire from the breadboard GND rail to the power supply ground terminal.

steps.title: Connect VCC Jumper Wire
steps.instruction: Connect a red jumper wire from the VCC positive bus line to the power supply 5V terminal.

common_mistakes.explanation: The wire is connected to the GND rail instead of the VCC rail.
common_mistakes.correction_action: Move the jumper wire from the blue GND rail to the red VCC rail.

steps.title: Verify Voltage Drop Across Resistor
steps.instruction: Use a multimeter to measure the voltage drop across the 220Ω resistor. Expected reading: approximately 2.8V.

steps.title: Power Circuit and Observe
steps.instruction: Switch the power supply ON and confirm the LED illuminates bright red. If not, check all connections and polarity.
